title: Indians Lead UK Visa, Settlement, and Citizenship Numbers Across All Major Routes
excerpt: Official UK government data shows Indian nationals account for nearly one in five visas issued, top the list for work-based settlement, and rank first for British citizenship grants among non-EU nationalities.
body:
• Indian nationals received 165,970 UK visas in the year ending June 2025, accounting for 19.9% of all visas issued — the highest of any nationality
  • Indians led work-related settlement grants with 21,696 in the year ending March 2026, driven primarily by the Skilled Worker route
  • India, Pakistan, and Nigeria were the top three nationalities for British citizenship grants, together accounting for nearly a quarter of all grants
  • Despite Indians leading across legal immigration categories, overall UK visa numbers have dropped 32% year-on-year

Indian nationals have emerged as the dominant nationality across virtually every legal immigration pathway in the United Kingdom, leading visa grants, work-based settlement, and British citizenship applications, according to the latest official data from the UK Home Office and the Office for National Statistics.

The data, compiled from multiple releases covering the years ending June 2025 through June 2026, paints a picture of a community deeply embedded in Britain's workforce, education system, and path to permanent residency.

One in Five UK Visas Go to Indians

In the year ending June 2025, a total of 834,977 visas were issued to foreign nationals to enter the UK for employment, study, family, or humanitarian reasons. Indian nationals received the largest share — 165,970 visas, or 19.9% of the total, according to Home Office data.

China ranked second with 114,128 visas (13.7%), followed by Pakistan (69,580, 8.3%), Nigeria (45,966, 5.5%), and the United States (30,898, 3.7%). The overall number of UK visas has fallen sharply, dropping 32% from 1.23 million in the year ending June 2024 to 835,000 in the year ending June 2025.

In more recent data covering the year ending June 2026, China slightly edged ahead of India for sponsored study visas specifically, with 86,000 grants compared to India's 83,000, though the two countries together accounted for 46% of all study visas issued.

Settlement: Indians Top Work Route

When it comes to settling permanently in the UK, Indians again led the field. In the year ending March 2026, Indian nationals received the highest number of work-related settlement grants at 21,696, according to UK government statistics. This was followed by Turkish nationals at 5,395 and Nigerians at 5,105.

The Skilled Worker route accounted for the bulk of these grants, with 53,203 total grants across all nationalities — a 7% increase from the prior year. Work-related settlement grants overall reached 67,699 in the period, even as total settlement grants declined 11% to 152,306, driven by drops in family and refugee categories.

Family-related settlement was most common among Pakistani nationals (6,688), followed by Indian (3,195) and Nigerian (2,535) nationals.

Citizenship: India Leads Non-EU Grants

India also claimed the top spot for British citizenship grants. In the year ending March 2026, there were 236,512 grants of British citizenship, with India, Pakistan, and Nigeria as the top three nationalities, together accounting for nearly a quarter of all grants. Among non-EU nationals specifically, these three countries represented 30% of all citizenship grants.

The citizenship numbers reflect earlier settlement patterns — Indians who entered the UK on skilled worker visas in previous years are now completing the pathway to permanent residency and citizenship. The UK government's 2025 Migrant Journey report shows that a significant proportion of work-route migrants are granted settlement after five years, feeding into subsequent citizenship applications.

What the Numbers Mean for the Indian Diaspora

A separate report by Aston University and Here & Now 365, unveiled at the House of Lords earlier this year, found that the Indian community has become the most economically successful migrant group in the United Kingdom. The report highlighted high employment levels, strong educational attainment, and a deep-rooted culture of entrepreneurship.

"The Indian diaspora is woven into the UK's growth story. Indian-led enterprises, research initiatives, and professional networks are generating employment, boosting skills development, and fostering knowledge exchange in communities across the nation."

— Aston University and Here & Now 365 Report

Indian-born professionals currently account for an estimated 15% of Britain's technology workforce, and the community has the highest homeownership rate among ethnic groups in the UK at 71%, according to a Policy Exchange analysis of 2021 census data.

The data arrives at a time of significant policy shifts in UK immigration. While overall visa numbers are declining — work visas fell 62% from their December 2023 peak and Health and Care Worker visas dropped 90% — Indian nationals continue to lead in extensions and new applications across categories, reflecting their established role in Britain's healthcare, technology, and education sectors.
